facts: Jiuyao Lu, Georgy Noarov, and Aaron Roth authored 'Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity', posted to arXiv on 2026-11-02 (arxiv:2611.03305).
Calibrated multiaccuracy requires a predictor to be globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family G, meaning its residuals are uncorrelated with every test g(x) in G.
Full multicalibration has sample complexity of ~Θ(log|G|/ε^2 + 1/ε^3) when |G| is at least a sufficiently large power of log(1/ε).
The authors show the sample complexity of ε-calibrated multiaccuracy for randomized predictors scales as ~Θ(log|G|/ε^2 + 1/ε^(5/2)), separating it from full multicalibration.
For deterministic predictors where log|G| = Ω(log(1/ε)), the tight sample complexity rate is established as ~Θ(log|G|/ε^2 + (log|G|)^(1/3)/ε^(8/3)).
When log|G| ≤ ε^(-1+κ) for fixed κ ∈ (0, 1), the deterministic sample complexity is polynomially larger than the randomized sample complexity, creating a genuine separation.
The matching upper and lower bounds prove that the cube-root dependence on log|G| for deterministic predictors is intrinsic.
When log|G| ≍ ε^(-1), the minimax sample complexity rates for both randomized and deterministic calibrated multiaccuracy coincide with the minimax rate for full multicalibration.
